subject: PayLoop: production retry spike and mitigation plan
messages:
From: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@payloop.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Production errors: surge of 5xx/429 after billing rollout

Hi Ben,

We pushed a billing rollout about 30 minutes ago and immediately started seeing elevated 5xx/429 responses from the Redwood API. Customers are seeing timeouts and repeated retries on our side. Attaching a short sample of the error payloads and a small trace bundle.

Key facts:
- Region: us-west-2
- SDK in use: payloop-frontend v1.3.0 (we haven't changed the SDK)
- Errors: mixture of 500s and 429s, spikes align with our job that replays charges
- We see lots of identical requests with identical request ids in short succession (possible retry loop)

Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side and whether you can throttle at the API key level? We need a short-term mitigation while we investigate.

Files attached: payloop-error-sample.json, replay-logs-20270521.tar.gz

Thanks,
Tim Saunders
Head of Integrations, PayLoop
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@payloop.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: surge of 5xx/429 after billing rollout

Hi Tim — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. We've triaged the sample and started a live investigation. A few quick asks so we don't waste cycles:

1) Can you confirm the exact client SDK version and whether you changed any retry/backoff settings with the rollout?
2) Do you have any server-side logs that show the timing of retries (client timestamps)?
3) Would you be open to us applying a short-term per-key smoothing/throttling policy (5–10s window) to reduce amplification while you patch?

I've looped in Marcus (runtime) and Neha (CS) to coordinate. We'll aim to set a mitigation within the hour if you give permission.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@payloop.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: surge of 5xx/429 after billing rollout

Tim / team — quick update from runtime. We ingested the replay-logs you sent and instrumented a short capture on the customer API key. Initial findings:

- There are repeat request bursts with the same payload and identical client request ids in sub-second intervals.
- The traffic pattern is consistent with an incorrect client-side retry/backoff loop (no exponential jitter).
- Downstream queues started saturating and we saw an uptick in contention -> internal 5xx amplification.

Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately (need your sign-off for per-key changes):
- Enable per-api-key smoothing: limit to 10 requests/second burst, with a token-bucket refill that allows normal traffic but caps amplification.
- Enable short-circuit 429 with Retry-After header when bursts exceed threshold so clients back off instead of retrying.
- Temporarily raise quota priority for PayLoop's background jobs (if you prefer fast completion) while we patch your SDK.

Longer-term we recommend you update SDK backoff to implement exponential backoff with full jitter and to add idempotency keys for the billing replay job. We'll share a small patch and recommended config.

If you authorize the per-key smoothing I will push config now and monitor for error rate reduction. Also sending the relevant logs to our incident channel.

Attachments: payloop-mitigation-playbook.md

— Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@payloop.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace Lim <grace.lim@payloop.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:53:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors: surge of 5xx/429 after billing rollout

Thanks Marcus — please apply the per-key smoothing and the 429/Retry-After behavior. We can flip the rollout back only if necessary, but prefer a live mitigation so customers aren't blocked. Confirming SDK: payloop-frontend v1.3.0 default retry behavior (linear backoff, 3 retries, no jitter). We'll push a hotfix to add exponential backoff + jitter — ETA 4 hours.

Grace and I will send you the exact timestamps for our replay job. Please call if you need immediate access to logs.

Tim
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec ask: PayLoop retry storm — approval for temporary throttle and service credit

Ava — FYI and request for quick approval. PayLoop experienced a retry amplification event after a billing rollout. Marcus is applying per-key smoothing and 429/Retry-After to stop the flood. They plan a client-side hotfix in ~4 hours.

Customer asks:
- Immediate per-key throttling (approved by customer)
- A 5% service credit for the hour of elevated errors (PayLoop is asking; not yet escalated to sales leadership)

We should approve the temporary mitigation and propose the 5% credit as a one-off goodwill gesture; Ben is on the thread to handle commercial follow-up.

I can attach the mitigation playbook and the logs sent by the customer.

Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exec ask: PayLoop retry storm — approval for temporary throttle and service credit

Thanks — good work moving quickly. Approve the per-key smoothing and 429/Retry-After mitigation.

Approve a one-time 5% credit for the hour of elevated errors; Ben, please document the credit in HubSpot and confirm with PayLoop. Marcus, keep monitoring for two hours post-patch and share a short RCA (root cause: client uncontrolled retries + missing jitter) and recommended config for SDK defaults.

Let's capture a short postmortem and a small docs update so SDK defaults favor exponential backoff + jitter by default. Put the playbook and logs into INF-981 and tag me.

Ava Chen
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
